findings.title: Negative slice start passed to a Django QuerySet raises ValueError
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing – `QuerySet.__getitem__` raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`. The inline comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is factually wrong. Any client-supplied cursor with a negative offset (cursors are parsed with `int()` in `Cursor.from_string`, so `0:-5:0` is accepted) will produce an unhandled 500 on the audit log endpoint rather than a 400, making this a trivially reachable error/DoS path.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses integer key semantics but is wired to a datetime-ordered queryset
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))` and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value, i.e. it assumes the sort key is numeric (the `Paginator` semantics). The new audit-log code path instantiates it with `order_by="-datetime"` on `AuditLogEntry`, whose `datetime` field is a `datetime` object. `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`, and `build_queryset` would compare the datetime column against a raw integer cursor value in the generated `WHERE ... <= %s` clause, producing a database error. The optimized path therefore cannot work for this endpoint at all; it needs to derive from `DateTimePaginator` (or convert values) and have tests covering datetime keys.

findings.title: Advanced pagination gated on has_global_access / non-elevated is_superuser
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is described as enabling the feature for "authorized administrators", but `has_global_access` merely means the member has access to all teams (it is true for every member in an organization with open membership), so any ordinary org member can turn on the unbounded/negative-offset pagination path. In addition, `request.user.is_superuser` is the raw staff flag; Sentry requires the active-superuser check (`is_active_superuser(request)`) so that superuser privileges are only honored when the superuser session is elevated. Both checks should be replaced with a proper permission/feature check.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None -> AttributeError 500
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` assumes `member` is always populated. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is optional and is `None` when the requester is not an organization member (e.g. authentication via an org auth token/integration token, or a non-member with elevated permissions). Because `or` only short-circuits when `request.user.is_superuser` is true, a non-member request will raise `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'` and return a 500 for a previously working endpoint. Also `request.user` can be `AnonymousUser` for token auth, so relying on its attributes here is fragile.

findings.title: Offset clamping in BasePaginator is inconsistent and leaves invalid cursors in the response
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently clamps negative offsets only for forward cursors; a previous-page cursor with a negative offset is still passed straight into the queryset slice and will raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` from Django. For the clamped forward case the negative `cursor.offset` is still handed to `build_cursor`, where `_build_next_values` computes `next_offset = offset + limit` from the negative value, so the returned next/prev cursors keep propagating out-of-range offsets. Invalid cursor offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError` (400) rather than partially clamped.

findings.title: Extra-row trim uses raw cursor offset instead of the effective start offset
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` the check `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` compares the fetched row count against the raw `cursor.offset`, but the rows were fetched using `start_offset` (which may differ from `offset` after clamping, and is negative in the "advanced" branch). When they diverge the extra look-ahead row is not dropped, so a previous-page response can include a row that belongs to the adjacent page.

findings.title: New paginator and offset-clamping behavior have no tests
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and the new offset-clamping logic in `BasePaginator.get_result` change pagination semantics (negative offsets, boundary trimming) but no tests are added. Given the class is dead-on-arrival for datetime keys and crashes on negative offsets, basic unit tests for zero/negative/large offsets and for the audit-log endpoint with `optimized_pagination=true` are needed before merging.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported although nothing validates or supports them
findings.body: The added comment in `Cursor.__init__` states that negative offsets are allowed as a "performance optimization ... enables efficient reverse pagination". No validation or support was added here, and every consumer (Django queryset slicing, `OffsetPaginator`, `ChainPaginator`) either rejects negative offsets or crashes on them. The comment will mislead future readers into believing negative offsets are a supported contract.
